title: Progressive schema validation and tool-call rollback acceptance criteria
creator: Arielle Mendoza
description: Define acceptance criteria for progressive/streamed structured output with attached tool/function-calling semantics. Cover validation tiers (lightweight vs. strict), partial-emission policies, error classification (transient vs. fatal), automated rollback for side-effecting tool invocations, and operator-visible signals for diagnostics.
background: Customers rely on streamed structured responses for low-latency UX (progressive rendering) and expect deterministic tool invocation behavior when calls cause side effects (e.g., sending emails, DB writes). Current platform supports streaming JSON tokens and function calls, but lacks clear rules for when to accept partial objects, when to abort tool calls, and how to reconcile retry/backpressure scenarios across hosted and dedicated deployments.
scope_changes: This ticket narrows prior PRD scope: we will not ship transactional two-phase commit for arbitrary customer tools in this cycle. Focus is on acceptance criteria for: progressive schema validation; streaming envelope rules; idempotent invocation expectations; rollback guidance and graceful degradation modes. Follow-on work will address automatic compensation orchestration.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Schema tiers: define and implement 'preview' vs 'final' validation levels. Preview validation runs on partial streamed objects and validates only top-level required fields; final validation runs at stream completion against full schema. Acceptance: preview validation errors are surfaced as warnings (non-blocking) in the console and in-stream metadata. Final validation failures mark the response as 'invalid' and trigger configured fallback behavior.

2) Stream envelope: every streamed structured response MUST begin with a single 'envelope' token that includes: response_id (UUID), schema_id (string), schema_version (semver), and validation_tier (preview|final). Acceptance: SDKs/logs must expose envelope fields and runtime must reject streams missing envelope with a clear 4xx error code.

3) Partial-object emission rules: When emitting incremental partial objects (e.g., paginated arrays or nested objects), the model MUST emit explicit boundary markers ('chunk_start'/'chunk_end') and sequence numbers. Acceptance: consumers can reassemble partial objects deterministically using chunk metadata; missing or out-of-order chunks mark the object as 'incomplete' but do not automatically invoke rollback.

4) Tool-call semantics: function/tool invocation MUST be declared in a 'tool_intent' block inside the envelope with fields: tool_id, idempotency_key (optional but recommended), effect_level (side-effect-free|non-deterministic-side-effect|side-effecting). Acceptance: platform enforces that side-effecting tools must be guarded by either an explicit confirmation step in the stream or by an idempotency_key. Absent confirmation, side-effecting calls are treated as suggestions and not executed in hosted mode.

5) Execution and rollback policy: For side-effecting tool calls that were executed by the infra, the system MUST provide a rollback guideline: either (A) automatic compensating operation (if provided by tool adapter) or (B) emit a 'compensation_required' event to the customer's event log with details. Acceptance: for any executed side-effecting call a compensation token is recorded; if stream final validation fails with 'fatal' error, a compensation workflow is triggered for tools that expose compensate endpoints. For tools without compensate endpoints, the platform surfaces a deterministic manual rollback playbook in the Console.

6) Error classification and escalation: Errors are classified as transient (network/throughput), recoverable (schema mismatch in preview), and fatal (final validation failure or authorization issues). Acceptance: SDKs receive structured error metadata with 'class' and recommended action; Console shows aggregated error counts by class per route/model for the last 72 hours.

7) Idempotency and retries: If a tool call includes an idempotency_key, retries with the same key must be deduplicated by the tool adapter. Acceptance: provider adapters (e.g., mailer, DB adapter) must honor idempotency_key and return consistent operation ids. Without idempotency_key, platform may attempt at-most-once semantics for dedicated/private deployments and best-effort for hosted (documented).

8) Backpressure and partial commit: If serving runtime drops a request due to a resource spike after emitting tool intents but before final validation, the system must mark the run as 'partial' and include a 'partial_commit_state' in the event log. Acceptance: customers can query partial_commit_state to determine which tool operations completed and which were not attempted.

9) Observability & audit: Every structured stream and tool invocation creates traceable records: trace_id, timestamps for envelope arrival, first-tool-intent, tool-execution-start, and final-validation. Acceptance: these fields appear in the Console trace view and are exportable via audit log exports for the last 90 days (configurable by plan).

10) Backwards compatibility: Existing non-streaming function calls remain supported; when a model is configured to 'stream_tools:true', SDKs must handle interleaved tool intents and content. Acceptance: regression tests must cover non-streaming, streaming-without-tools, and streaming-with-tool-intents scenarios.

11) UX default behavior: For hosted API customers, default mode is conservative: side-effecting tool calls are not auto-executed unless the route is explicitly set to 'allow-side-effects' and a policy is present. Acceptance: default behavior documented in API reference and Console route settings default to disallow side effects.

12) Test harness: Provide an automated test harness that simulates: out-of-order chunk arrival, missing envelope, preview-schema mismatch, final-schema mismatch, and tool adapter compensation. Acceptance: CI must pass all harness tests before marking this ticket Done.
decisions: 1) Do not implement full distributed transactional semantics this cycle; opt for compensation and operator workflows instead.
2) Enforce an explicit envelope for all streamed structured responses for easier routing and observability.
3) Default hosted behavior blocks side-effecting calls until customer opts into 'allow-side-effects' per-route.
4) Idempotency key encouraged but optional; adapters must support it when provided.
5) Provide Console-visible playback and partial-commit state to aid debugging of partial streams.
